title: Developing Christlike Attributes
focus: Practice topic: showing Christlike attributes with a companion
intro: A missionary wears the Savior’s name. In this lesson learners study why Christlike attributes matter, how they grow, and how they help a missionary teach and serve a companion in peace.
preparation: Study Alma 17:22–37; 18:1–3, 8–10; Moroni 7:45–48; and Doctrine and Covenants 4:1–7. Read the chapter on Christlike attributes in the missionary manual. Pray for each learner by name.

sections.title: Why Christlike attributes matter
paras: Look at a missionary name tag together. Two names stand out: the missionary’s own and the Savior’s. Ask why it matters that others link our name with His.

Read 3 Nephi 27:27. Ask how we accept the Savior’s invitation to follow Him. Draw out the truth: we follow Jesus Christ as we become like Him. Ask how this could make a missionary a stronger minister.

sections.title: How Christlike attributes grow
paras: Let each learner choose one verse about following the Savior and share what it says. Then ask which attributes they link with Him and where they saw them in His life.

Read Doctrine and Covenants 4:1–7. Ask how verses 5–6 connect our attributes to our qualification to serve. Read Moroni 7:47–48 and talk about how charity is a gift we ask for and then act on. Say it plainly: Christlike attributes are gifts from God. We seek them through prayer, repentance, faith in the Atonement and daily choices.

Give learners quiet time to pick one attribute and study it. They write: what is new to me, what must change in my heart or actions, and how this will help me as a missionary. Ask them to write a simple plan with one choice they can make each day.

sections.title: Attributes in missionary work
paras: Ask: How can we preach the gospel without words? What happens to a person’s heart when they are treated the way the Savior would treat them? Let learners list the attributes that investigators notice most.

Study Ammon in Alma 17:22–25, 28–31, 33–37 and Alma 18:1–3, 8–10. Each learner reads one section and finds the attributes Ammon showed. Ask how those attributes touched the people he served and how a missionary today could do the same. End by asking learners to think of someone who showed these attributes to them.

sections.title: Serving with a companion
paras: Ask: What can make it hard to serve with a companion? Why do missionaries serve in pairs? Read Doctrine and Covenants 42:6 and 2 Corinthians 13:1 to show the strength of two witnesses.

Read Doctrine and Covenants 38:24–25, 27 and 3 Nephi 11:29. Ask what happens to the Spirit when there is contention, and which attributes help companions stay united, such as patience, humility and love. Ask how unity makes a pair more effective in teaching.

steps.why: Teach the idea and why it matters for a missionary.

examples.title: Name the attribute
examples.text: Write an attribute on the board, such as patience, humility or charity. Show where one verse describes it, then say what it looks like in a missionary’s day.

examples.title: Show how attributes grow
examples.text: List four steps: ask, repent, act, repeat. Use Moroni 7:47–48 to show that we pray for charity and then live it.

examples.title: Show Ammon’s example
examples.text: Read Alma 17:28–31 and name two attributes Ammon showed. Say how a missionary could do the same.

steps.why: Show one example of what learners will do.

examples.title: Teach one attribute in three minutes
examples.text: Define the attribute, read one verse, share a simple example and invite a plan. Add a short testimony.

examples.title: Show a kind reply to a companion
examples.text: A companion is late and everyone feels tense. Show a calm, kind response that protects the spirit of the companionship.

examples.title: Show how to set a goal
examples.text: Write a goal that names an attribute, a daily action and a time. Share it aloud.

steps.why: Learners practise in pairs or small groups.

examples.title: Teach in pairs
examples.text: Each learner teaches one attribute for three minutes using a verse and an example from Ammon or the Savior.

examples.title: Role-play a hard moment
examples.text: One plays a companion who is frustrated. The other responds with a Christlike attribute.

examples.title: Write a personal plan
examples.text: Each learner picks one attribute and writes one action for each day this week.

steps.why: Name what went well and what can improve.

examples.title: Partner feedback
examples.text: The learner who was taught says what was clearest and what felt most sincere. The teacher writes one thing to keep and one to improve.

examples.title: Three questions
examples.text: Ask: What went well? What would you change? What helped the listener most to understand Christlike attributes? Begin with the good.

examples.title: Simple checklist
examples.text: Was it simple? Was a scripture used and explained? Was the listener invited to act? Did the teacher speak with sincerity?

steps.why: Practise again with what was learned.

examples.title: Switch roles
examples.text: The learner who listened now teaches. Leave time for feedback both ways, then ask a few to share what they learned.

examples.title: Improve one thing
examples.text: Each learner teaches again and changes one thing from the feedback: a clearer sentence, a better scripture or a warmer invitation.

examples.title: Teach a new partner
examples.text: Find a new partner. Teach the same lesson again in a few minutes. Share one insight with the class.

testimony: Share how a Christlike person has blessed your life. Testify that the Savior helps us become more like Him as we try.

tips.text: Give learners quiet time to think before you ask for answers. Thoughtful answers take a moment.
Help learners write down what they will do. Application grows when feelings become a plan.
Invite learners to share a real experience, and thank them for it.
Ask learners to name an attribute and then act on it this week.

quote.text: What manner of men ought ye to be? Verily I say unto you, even as I am.

study: Read Moroni 7:47–48 together and ask what we are asked to do to receive charity.
invitations: Choose one Christlike attribute and study it with the scriptures, the Bible Dictionary and the Topical Guide.
Ask how you can be more Christlike toward your family, friends and neighbors.
Set goals to prevent contention with a future companion.
Find ways to show love to family and friends and to serve them.
